title: 第五章 笔与纸
content_zh:
那一夜，江砚疼得几乎没合眼。

    破屋四面漏风，他把那床结成疙瘩的破棉絮裹得紧紧的，蜷在草堆里，浑身上下没一处不疼。后背被棍子打出几道紫红的印子，肋骨那里一呼吸就抽痛，他怀疑断了一两根。

    可比身上的疼更折磨人的，是脑子里那笔账。

    五日。三贯钱，五石粮。

    在现代，这点钱算什么？他随手就能凑出来。可在这里，对一个一无所有的乡下孤儿来说，这就是一道根本迈不过去的坎。五日后，等着他的只有两条路：要么被绑去林家庄子做牛做马，活活累死；要么，他得想出个法子。

    江砚翻来覆去，把原主的记忆又筛了一遍，想从里头淘出点能用的东西。

    筛到后半夜，他还真淘出来一样。

    ——他识字。

    原主的爹江守文，早年在镇上私塾给人帮工，认得几个字。原主七岁前，江守文常把他抱在膝头，拿树枝在地上教他写。后来江守文死了，没人再教，可那点底子，原主一直没忘——夜里没事，他常蹲在地上，用手指头默写那些字，像是借此还能摸到一点爹的温度。

    在这个十里八村识字的人都数得过来的地方，“识字”，就是一门吃饭的本事。

    江砚精神一振。

    天蒙蒙亮，他忍着浑身的疼爬起来，在破屋里翻找。原主的家当少得可怜，可在一个糊着泥的墙洞里，他还是摸出了一个用油布裹了好几层的小包袱——那是江守文留下的、原主藏得最深的念想。

    打开来，里头是一方豁了角的旧砚台、一截只剩半寸长的秃笔，还有几片裁得歪歪扭扭、写过字又被刮干净的旧麻纸。

    江砚捏着那截秃笔，心里头说不出是什么滋味。

    他这辈子最烦写字。可阴差阳错，到了这地方，能让他活命的，偏偏就是这支笔。

    他往豁角的砚台里倒了点水——墨是没有的，只有半块原主不知从哪儿捡来的、干硬的旧墨头，他对着哈了几口气，就着冻疮裂口渗出的那点热乎气，在砚台里费劲地磨。磨了半天，才磨出一点浅淡得几乎看不见的墨汁。

    他蘸了墨，铺开一片旧麻纸，准备先试试这具身子的手，还认不认得字。

    可笔尖一落到纸上，江砚就皱起了眉。

    这具身子的手，太僵了。冻疮、旧伤、加上长年劳作落下的颤，让他连一道横都拉不直。写出来的字，歪歪扭扭，缺胳膊少腿，比他现代那手“鬼画符”还不如。

    “……废了。”他低声骂了一句。

    越写越烦。五日的限期像座山压在心口，债、伤、饿、冷，一桩桩一件件，搅得他心烦意乱。笔下那几个字，他写得越来越快，越来越乱，到后来，索性破罐破摔，由着那股憋闷劲儿，一笔不停地在纸上狂涂乱画起来。
content_en:
That night, Jiang Yan was in so much pain that he could barely sleep a wink.

    The dilapidated house was drafty from all sides, so he wrapped the bed tightly with the knotted cotton wool and huddled in the hay. Every part of his body hurt. There were several purple-red marks on his back from the stick, and his ribs throbbed every time he breathed. He suspected that one or two of them were broken.

    But what was more torturous than the pain in my body was the account in my mind.

    Five days. Three guans of money, five shi of grain.

    In modern times, what does this little money mean? He can just pull it together. But here, for a country orphan with nothing, this is a hurdle that is simply impossible to overcome. Five days later, there were only two options waiting for him: Either he would be kidnapped to work as a cow or a horse in Linjiazhuang, and he would die from exhaustion; or, he would have to find a way.

    Jiang Yan turned over and over again, sifting through the memory of the original owner, trying to find something useful from it.

    After sifting through it until the middle of the night, it looked like he had actually found it.

    ——He can read.

    The original owner's father, Jiang Shouwen, worked as a helper in a private school in the town in his early years and knew a few words. Before the original owner was seven years old, Jiang Shouwen often held him on his knees and put branches on the ground to teach him to write. Later, Jiang Shouwen died and no one taught him anymore, but the original owner never forgot that basic knowledge - at night, he would often squat on the ground and write the words silently with his fingers, as if he could feel a little of his father's warmth.

    In this place where the number of literate people in eight villages within ten miles can be counted, "literacy" means the ability to eat.

    Jiang Yan perked up.

    At dawn, he endured the pain all over his body and got up, rummaging through the shabby house. The original owner's belongings were pitiful, but in a muddy wall hole, he still found a small bundle wrapped several layers of oilcloth - it was Jiang Shouwen's deepest thought that the original owner had hidden.

    When he opened it, he found inside an old inkstone with a chipped corner, a bald pen that was only half an inch long, and a few crooked pieces of old hemp paper that had been written on and then scraped clean.

    Jiang Yan held the bald piece of pen and couldn't tell what he felt in his heart.

    Writing is the most annoying thing in his life. But by mistake, when he got to this place, the thing that could keep him alive was this pen.

    He poured some water into the inkstone at the cracked corner - there was no ink, only half of an old dry ink tip that the original owner had picked up from somewhere. He breathed a few times and rubbed it hard in the inkstone with the heat oozing out of the frostbite cracks. After grinding for a long time, I got out a little ink that was so light that it was almost invisible.

    He dipped it in ink and spread out a piece of old hemp paper, ready to test the body's hands to see if he could read the words.

    But as soon as the pen tip landed on the paper, Jiang Yan frowned.

    The hands of this body are too stiff. Frostbite, old injuries, and the tremors from years of toil left him unable to straighten even a single line. The handwriting was crooked and missing arms and legs, worse than his modern "ghost-drawing" hand.

    "...It's useless." He cursed in a low voice.

    The more I write, the more annoying I get. The five-day deadline was like a mountain weighing on his heart. Debt, injury, hunger, and cold were all one after another, making him upset. He wrote the few words he wrote faster and faster, and became more and more messy. Finally, he simply broke the can and started scribbling wildly on the paper with his suppressed energy.
